advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _foldable_event_count skip events whose event_type is not in KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES, matching _parse_candidate_events, so selection cannot drift above what the fold squashes.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:166: `if name.startswith(".") or not name.endswith(".json") or name.endswith("-SYNC.json"):` — the only exclusions; event_type is never read
src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:170: `raw_ts = json.load(fh).get("timestamp")` — reads only timestamp, not event_type
src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:200: `if etype and etype not in KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES:` followed by `continue` — the fold drops unknown-type events from its candidate set

docstring at src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:156 claims 'Matches the fold's candidate set: *.json, excluding dotfiles, already-retired sources and -SYNC.json' but omits the unknown-type filter the fold applies
advisory.finding: _foldable_event_count counts forward-compat unknown-type events as foldable, but the fold (_parse_candidate_events) drops any event whose event_type is not in KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES. Selection therefore over-counts relative to what the fold squashes, so a ticket whose over-horizon events are predominantly unknown-type can be selected, fold nothing new, be reported 'nothing to fold', and be re-selected on every subsequent sweep — the churn the docstring claims is impossible because 'selection and the fold ask one question through one predicate'.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _foldable_event_count, read event_type alongside timestamp and `continue` when `etype and etype not in KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES`, mirroring _parse_candidate_events.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the ticket's own -SNAPSHOT.json should count toward the foldable total; if not, exclude `-SNAPSHOT.json` in _foldable_event_count to match operator expectation and avoid threshold-0 churn.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:166: exclusion list does not exclude `-SNAPSHOT.json`
tests/interfaces/contracts/test_event_schema_forward_compat.py:94: `assert "SNAPSHOT" in _version.KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` — SNAPSHOT is a known/foldable type
src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:224: `if foldable > threshold or (foldable > 0 and not has_snapshot):` — at threshold=0 an aged SNAPSHOT alone gives foldable==1>0
src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:238: fold retires old sources and writes a new SNAPSHOT, so re-selection re-folds forever at threshold 0
advisory.finding: _foldable_event_count counts the ticket's own `-SNAPSHOT.json` toward the foldable event total (SNAPSHOT is a KNOWN_EVENT_TYPE and its filename ends in .json, so it is not excluded). This inflates the foldable count by one and, at threshold 0 (the historical default arg and the offline-suite setting), makes a fully-settled ticket that holds only an aged SNAPSHOT satisfy `foldable > 0` and be re-selected each sweep, re-folding the SNAPSHOT into a new SNAPSHOT indefinitely.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile docs/concurrency.md's "its own `.git`" claim with the workflow mounting the store as a worktree (shared `.git`) rather than a standalone clone.
evidence: docs/concurrency.md: "on a disposable CI runner: its own clone, its own `.git`, its own index and its own store write lock"
.github/workflows/compact-sweep.yml: "git worktree add -B tickets .tickets-tracker origin/tickets" under step "Mount tickets branch as a worktree"
advisory.finding: docs/concurrency.md claims the sweep runs in a clone with "its own `.git`, its own index", but the workflow mounts the store as a git worktree (`git worktree add -B tickets .tickets-tracker origin/tickets`) of the CI checkout, which shares the parent checkout's `.git` object store rather than having its own.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that monkeypatches compact_cli to return non-zero for one ticket and asserts compact_all_cli returns 2, prints 'E', and lists the errored ticket id on stderr.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:378 `if rc != 0:` then `error_ids.append(tid)` / `sys.stdout.write("E")`
src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:404 `return 2 if error_ids else 0`
.github/workflows/compact-sweep.yml: `if [ "${rc:-0}" = "2" ]; then echo "::warning::some tickets failed to compact..." elif [ "${rc:-0}" != "0" ]; then exit "${rc}"`

ABSENCE: `search_files` for `error_ids` and `Errored tickets` across tests/ returns (no matches); existing tests assert only `in (0, 2)` (tests/unit/test_compact_all_selection.py:199,203) without ever forcing an error
advisory.finding: The exit-code-2 error path of compact_all_cli is untested. The new compact-sweep.yml workflow branches on exit 2 (surface a warning, do not fail the run) versus exit 1 (fail), but no test exercises a ticket whose per-ticket fold returns rc != 0, so the accumulation of error_ids, the 'E' progress marker, the 'Errored tickets' stderr listing, and the `return 2 if error_ids else 0` contract are all unverified.
scenarios: A ticket's fold raises/returns non-zero mid-sweep on CI; the workflow must warn (exit 2) rather than fail the run — a regression that flipped this to exit 1 (or 0) would go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: In tests/unit/test_compact_all_selection.py add a test seeding two foldable tickets, monkeypatching _compact.compact_cli so one tid returns 1, asserting the call returns 2, that 'Errored tickets' and the failing tid appear in captured stderr, and that the succeeding ticket is still counted compacted.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a failure notification (and/or CloudWatch metric) step to compact-sweep.yml so a silently broken sole compaction trigger is observable, matching reconcile-bridge.yml.
evidence: compact-sweep.yml header: 'This is the store's ONLY standing compaction trigger'
compact-sweep.yml ends at the 'Run the sweep' step (line 154) with no failure() step
reconcile-bridge.yml:273 '- name: Notify on bridge failure\n        if: failure()'
reconcile-bridge.yml:367 'Publish bridge run failure to CloudWatch' and :335-339 comment: 'the failure surfaced only as an ::error annotation nobody was looking at'
src/rebar/_store/push.py:747-752 'except Exception: logger.warning("best-effort tickets-branch push failed; PUSH_PENDING will surface via fsck") ... return'
compact-sweep.yml header: 'a failed push leaves only local commits on a workspace that is discarded'
compact-sweep.yml:149 'rebar compact-all "${ARGS[@]}" || rc=$?' — only rc 1/2 are inspected; a swallowed push failure returns rc 0
advisory.finding: compact-sweep.yml — the store's declared ONLY standing compaction trigger — has no failure notification or telemetry step, unlike its stated template reconcile-bridge.yml which has both a 'Notify on bridge failure' step and CloudWatch put-metric-data steps. A silently broken schedule (expired REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY/token, pip install failure, worktree-mount failure) fails invisibly, letting event logs grow unbounded with no operator signal.
merged_from: A best-effort push failure in `rebar compact-all` (push_after_commit logs a warning and returns without raising, except for OptionalDependencyError) leaves the folded SNAPSHOTs only as local commits in a disposable clone that is then discarded, and the workflow still reports success — so a delivery failure of a completed fold is invisible at the run level.
scenarios: The bot token or checkout credentials expire; the scheduled sweep fails every 6h and no ticket is ever folded again, silently, until logs bloat
pip install -e . breaks on a dependency change; the sweep exits 1 with no alert
